answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable stake held in a shared vault, rather than to a free username. Creating one identity costs real copper-equivalent collateral that is slashed if the agent misbehaves, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues slowly to that staked identity, like wind shaping a path: a zephyr may pass quickly, but a durable record cannot be faked overnight. Newcomers start with limited permissions and earn more only through consistent, checkable work.
